prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1021; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a left-turn collision at an intersection and states that the other vehicle, which was approaching from the opposite direction, struck the driver's side. The driver is named on the policy, and the claimant is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Claimant reports a wrist fracture from the impact and was first seen at an urgent care facility. The reported injury is consistent with a collision of this type.

Entry 3: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent eyewitness to the collision itself has been identified so far.

Entry 4: Scene photographs were reviewed and confirm some of the described positions and points of impact. Vehicle damage is largely consistent with the impact the claimant described.

Entry 5: Claimant gave the same account of how the collision happened in each conversation so far, including the direction of travel and the sequence of events. No discrepancies have been noted.

Entry 6: Treatment has followed a typical course for this type of fracture, with follow-up visits spaced out as healing progressed. Claimant reports steady improvement and fewer visits are now scheduled.

Entry 7: Medical history review found no earlier injury to the same wrist or arm. Claimant's records do not show prior treatment for that area.

Entry 8: Vehicle history check found no prior damage to the claimant's car on file. Repair estimate was requested and is pending review.

Entry 9: A neighbor contacted the office and believes the car already had damage some weeks before the claimed collision. This statement has not been verified and will be followed up with the neighbor and with the repair shop.

Entry 10: Open items include the neighbor's statement, the final repair estimate, and the treating provider's discharge summary. File will remain open until these items are reviewed.
